author: repair lane; not review, not qualification, not a seal
purpose: Repair the ONE blocking finding of c2-plan-stage-schema.v6.review-independent.json, IR-C2V6-01, and the documentation defects that review and the coordinator recorded with it. v6 is very nearly right and is NOT rewritten: jx_canon survived a direct attack of 82,368 distinct tokens with zero collisions, the primitive stands alone, the 109-row matrix ran to termination green with zero escapes and zero COUNTER-ONLY rows, and an independent sweep of 137 candidate mutations admitted none. All of that is preserved. What failed is one level below all of it: every layer of v6 operates on the PARSED OBJECT and nothing read the candidate's RAW BYTES, so eighteen bytes inserted into the v6 document put a JSON float at the one key whose integer-ness the checker enforces by an explicit named rule, and the run stayed fully green. v7 makes the PARSE a gate, puts that gate inside the portable primitive so an adopter cannot take the comparison and leave the parse behind, and asserts structurally over its own syntax tree that every JSON parse in the file goes through it.

resolves.IR-C2V4-01: REPAIRED, inherited from the v5 lane and re-established here by execution. The three ungated census comparisons are replaced by a comparator whose single acceptance path asserts the JSON type of both operands and then compares CANONICAL STRINGS, so no numeric operator runs. The position set is derived from the live measurement in both directions.
resolves.IR-C2V5-01: REPAIRED. The defect was `if not adjudicated <= lines:` at check-c2-v5.py line 1815 -- a set-subset test where a wire operand met a computed integer set, admitted because `{2487} <= {2487.0}` is True and invisible because v5's taint model laundered the name bound to a comprehension RESULT. Three things change: the comparison is jx_subset over canonical tokens; every repairedComparisonSites line is type-asserted and named individually before any comparison; and L4's taint model now propagates through comprehension, generator and container-constructor results, which is demonstrated by running v7's scan over the PINNED check-c2-v5.py, where it reports line 1815 that v5's own scan reported clean. The vector itself is retained as a live L6c case executed against the pinned v5 bytes on every run.
resolves.IR-C2V5-02: REPAIRED. v5 declared five type gates, broke two, and three could be stripped with zero findings. v7 declares its gates as the primitive's own entry points and L7 breaks EVERY one of them, each row asserting a specific finding id and the subject under test.
resolves.IR-C2V5-03: REPAIRED. L2c binds every integer leaf AND every JSON number leaf of THIS document to a value this run measured or to a byte of a hash-verified pinned input, with no unbound bucket: a leaf nobody binds is itself a named finding, so narrowing the binding table fails closed. retainedFalseAcceptVectors.measuredThisRun and theDefect.wholeDocumentSweep are inside the binding, not exempt from it, and every one of those leaves is probed with hostile spellings and arbitrary value drift on every run.
resolves.IR-C2V5-04: REPAIRED. L7 breaks every layer as well as every gate, including the anchor functions v5 left unbroken, and each break is re-run against a candidate whose every bound counter has been republished from the mutant's own measurements. A row whose finding survives only before republication is reported as COUNTER-ONLY and fails the suite, so no counter can be the sole detector of any break.
resolves.IR-C2V6-01: REPAIRED. main() did `candidate = json.loads(path.read_text())` with no object_pairs_hook. CPython keeps the LAST occurrence of a duplicated key, so inserting `  "version": 6.0,` immediately before the existing `  "version": 6,` produced a parsed object byte-for-byte identical to the parse of the unedited file: exit 0, full green banner, including the line certifying 105 integer leaves of THIS document bound with no unbound bucket, over a document of record carrying a float at the one key an explicit named rule requires to be a JSON integer. Four things change. The parse itself becomes a primitive gate, jx_loads, which returns the parse AND an explicit account of what the host threw away, and it covers duplicate keys at any depth, the non-RFC constants NaN and Infinity, and number tokens whose spelling is not the canonical spelling of their value. EVERY JSON input this checker loads goes through it, not only the candidate. A structural scan of this file's own syntax tree requires every json.load and json.loads call to pass an object_pairs_hook, with two named, counted exemptions that exist to reproduce the predecessor's own parse as evidence, so the property is over the whole tree instead of over a list of inputs somebody remembered. And the sha256 of the exact candidate bytes that were parsed is computed from those bytes and printed in the banner, so the verdict names the document it is a verdict about. The vector is retained as executable: the mechanism runs on every invocation as L8 against three pinned documents, and the full execution of the pinned, REJECTED check-c2-v6.py over the eighteen-byte edit is a retained --selftest row that must still find it FULLY GREEN.

wholeDocumentSweep.why: The brief and the adjudication both name three comparison sites. Three was NOT assumed to be the complete set.
wholeDocumentSweep.method: A float substituted at each integer leaf of the verified predecessor document in turn, each mutant driven through a complete check-c2-v4.py check() over the pinned Authority, on EVERY invocation of check-c2-v6.py.
wholeDocumentSweep.consequence: A repair scoped to the three census sites would have closed the census share and shipped the rest for the next reviewer to rediscover. The most pointed of the non-census positions is planIntent/integerConstantFields/fields/4/range/1: the upper bound inside the predecessor's own integer-constant register, the register whose stated purpose is that a fifth site cannot be added silently, is itself float-admissible. check-c2-v7.py requires the sweep to keep finding that position admitted, and three others like it, by name.
wholeDocumentSweep.whyThisIsNowExhaustive: v5 published these figures as literal banner text and range-tested the contract's copies between one and a million. The independent reviewer republished them as one and the run stayed green with the banner unchanged. A published measurement the run does not recompute and bind is not evidence, so every figure here is recomputed on every invocation and bound, the banner renders from the same register under the name of the thing each number measures, and the banner is structurally refused if it carries any bare digit as source text.

theDefect.whyThisIsBlockingAndNotAdvisory: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE section 7: the test is reachability on the actual bytes. The blind spot was OCCUPIED: the ungated comparison was already written, already reached on every ordinary invocation, and the evasion required editing only the input document.

theSuccessorDefect.summary: check-c2-v5.py line 1815 reads `if not adjudicated <= lines:`, where `lines` is a set built from the WIRE value item.get('line') and `adjudicated` is a set of integers parsed from the pinned adjudication. Set membership is hash-and-equality, so `{2487} <= {2487.0}` is True. One JSON edit, zero bytes of Python, no compensation: exit 0 and a full green banner including the line certifying zero type-distinct admissions. It is the third generation of the same fault, and it is not an equality comparison, which is why patching `!=` would not have closed it.
theSuccessorDefect.whyTheV5ScanCouldNotSeeIt: v5's taint fixpoint tainted comprehension TARGETS but never the name bound to a comprehension RESULT, so `lines` was laundered clean; and v5's non-numeric model excused set() and sorted() results as container comparisons rather than integer comparisons, when `{2487} <= {2487.0}` and `[1] == [1.0]` are both True. check-c2-v7.py's scan reports that line when run over the PINNED check-c2-v5.py, and the count is published.

theParseDefect.summary: check-c2-v6.py main() reads the candidate with `json.loads(path.read_text())` and no object_pairs_hook. CPython keeps the LAST occurrence of a duplicated key, so a shadowing key produces a parsed object that is byte-for-byte the parse of the unedited document. Every guard of v6, the comparison primitive included, operates on that parsed object; nothing in the checker reads the candidate's raw bytes. A reader of the file sees a float at `version`; every instrument sees an integer. It is not a defect in the primitive - jx_canon never sees the shadowed value at all - which is exactly why no amount of strengthening the comparison closes it.
theParseDefect.whyThePrimitiveCouldNotHaveCaughtIt: The primitive canonicalises a value it is GIVEN. v6 said so, and named the construction-time loss of equal-hashing dict keys as the blind spot, and correctly observed that a JSON parse cannot produce that case because object keys are always strings. The neighbouring construction-time loss that IS reachable from a parse is duplicate keys, and it was not named. The blind spot was one word away from the blocker.

minimalReproduction.reproducedPerRunDetail: STATED PRECISELY BECAUSE OVERCLAIMING HERE WOULD BE THE SAME DEFECT IN A NEW PLACE. An ordinary invocation of check-c2-v7.py recomputes the MECHANISM on every run: for each retained vector it edits the pinned document's bytes, executes the unhooked host parse exactly as the predecessor performs it, and requires that parse to be unable to distinguish the edited bytes from the unedited ones, while requiring its own parse to name the position. It also reads the pinned predecessor's own syntax tree and requires the number of its JSON parses that pass an object_pairs_hook to still be zero. What an ordinary invocation does NOT recompute is the full execution of check-c2-v6.py over the mutant, because that costs about eighty seconds and would double the cost of every run. That execution is a RETAINED --selftest ROW: the suite executes the pinned, rejected predecessor over the eighteen-byte edit and fails unless it is still FULLY GREEN. Retained as RES-C2V7-11.

v4InheritanceProjection.rule: check-c2-v4.py is pinned to a document declaring version 4, supersedes 3 and checker check-c2-v4.py. To execute it as an oracle over the effective v7 contract those three identity bytes are restored, and NOTHING else is. check-c2-v7.py admits exactly this field set and recomputes the full type-exact diff between the effective contract and the projection, refusing the run if it is not exactly these three paths.
v4InheritanceProjection.whyThisIsSafe: The three restored values are not read by any measurement. The contract-root path census is a function of document STRUCTURE and of which leaf values collide with the seven hostile injection values; none of these identity values collides with any of them.

thePrimitive.why: Every repair before v6 guarded call sites. v4 guarded the wire validator and left its census bare; v5 guarded the census and left its own repro enumeration bare. Each repair was a list of places and the defect moved to a place not on the list. v6 fixed that and built the primitive - and the defect moved BELOW it, to the parser, which is not a place on any list either and is the one boundary every layer inherits without choosing to. v7 keeps v6's design entirely and adds the parse to the primitive.
thePrimitive.whatItIs: jx_canon, a total, length-framed, type-tagged canonical encoding of a JSON value, and everything else defined in terms of it. Comparison, ordering, membership, key lookup, set algebra, dedup, sorting and extremes are all decided by STRING equality or STRING ordering over canonical tokens. v7 adds jx_loads, the PARSE, to the same block: the boundary at which the bytes become a value is a law-18 gate like any other, and an adopter who copies the block gets it rather than having to remember it.
thePrimitive.whyItIsSoundAndNotJustCareful: jx_canon is INVERTIBLE. jx_decanon reconstructs the original value exactly, type and all, which means jx_canon is injective, which means it can never give two distinct JSON values the same token. That is executed over the whole corpus on every run and the counts are published: corpus values, distinct tokens and round trips must all agree.
thePrimitive.theOperatorSpace: Equality, inequality and their operator.* call forms; ordering in both directions and their call forms; membership and non-membership over lists, tuples, sets and dict keys; key lookup by subscript, get, pop, setdefault and fromkeys; set algebra including subset, superset, disjointness, union, intersection and difference; dedup through set(), frozenset(), set literals and set and dict comprehensions; aggregation through sorted, min, max, sum and Counter; container equality at any depth, where [1] equals [1.0] and an object with an integer value equals the same object with the float; boolean-as-integer, where hash(True) equals hash(1); signed zero; foreign numeric types that compare equal to an integer; BARE TRUTHINESS, where bool(1), bool(1.0) and bool(True) are all the same value so `if x:` carries exactly the equivalence semantics this table exists to enumerate; %d STRINGIFICATION; and THE PARSE, where json.loads keeps the last duplicate key, accepts NaN and Infinity, and turns `-0` into 0 and `1E2` into 100.0. The last three groups are v7's: the truthiness and stringification rows were omitted from v6's table, which called itself the operator space, and the parse rows are IR-C2V6-01. Every row carries a live demonstration that the host-language hazard still reproduces AND a demonstration that the primitive answers differently, and both are executed on every run.
thePrimitive.whyTheContainerHalfMatters: hash(1), hash(1.0) and hash(True) are equal, so len({1, 1.0, True}) is 1. Three distinct JSON values silently become one, and a cardinality published from that set is a false measurement that no equality guard would ever see. This is why the repair could not be a wider list of comparison operators.
thePrimitive.shouldACheckerCompareAMeasuredValueAgain: The comparison exists to catch contract drift and it is also what creates the false-accept surface. v7 keeps the comparison and removes the surface: jx_bind asserts the JSON type of each side independently and FIRST, then compares canonical strings. No numeric operator runs, so there is no coercion path to defend. The residual risk is no longer numeric; it is that the measurement function measures the wrong space, which is RES-C2V6-04 and is a different failure mode.
thePrimitive.whatThePrimitiveCannotDo: It canonicalises a value it is GIVEN, and v7 moves the boundary of that sentence rather than repeating it. The host language collapses equal-hashing dict keys at CONSTRUCTION: the object literal mapping 1, true and 1.0 to three different values is already a one-entry object by the time any gate runs. jx_keyset and jx_unique close that for sequences, and a JSON parse cannot produce it because object keys are always strings - which v6 stated correctly, and which was one word away from IR-C2V6-01, because the NEIGHBOURING construction-time loss is duplicate keys and that one IS reachable from a parse. jx_loads closes it. What remains is an internally built map that loses information upstream of the gate, which is measured and declared rather than mitigated.
thePrimitive.portability: The primitive is delimited in the source by BEGIN and END markers and the delimited region is verified on every run to have no free name outside its declared portability boundary, so it can be copied into another checker verbatim. That is a coverage claim and is held to the same standard as any other: the count is measured and published.
whatAnAdoptingCheckerMustDo: Copy the delimited region and jx_selftest. Call jx_selftest from your own run, fail closed unless its escapes list is empty, and publish its counts.

PARSE EVERY JSON INPUT WITH jx_loads, not only the one you call the candidate, and emit a named finding at the position for every problem it reports. Then copy json_load_sites and require every json.load and json.loads in YOUR tree to pass an object_pairs_hook: the property has to be structural, because a parse defence applied to one input and not to its siblings is the list-of-places failure this lineage exists to escape. This step is IR-C2V6-01.

Replace every wire-touching equality, inequality, ordering, membership and subset with the jx equivalent; replace subscript and get on wire keys with jx_get or jx_at; replace set() and set literals over wire values with jx_keyset or jx_unique.

Replace sorted over wire values with jx_sorted, WHICH ORDERS A HETEROGENEOUS JSON TYPE SET BY CANONICAL TOKEN AND DOES NOT REFUSE ONE, or with jx_sorted_homogeneous, which refuses it by name. Replace min and max with jx_min and jx_max, which refuse a mixed type set, an empty sequence, a non-orderable JSON type and a non-finite number, each by name. Do NOT take an extreme off jx_sorted: token order is not value order, because the length prefix sorts first, so jx_sorted([3, -5]) is [3, -5].
Compare a published counter against a measured one with jx_bind ONLY, and a published string with jx_bind_text.

Copy wire_comparison_scan and run it over your own tree. Drive the ungated count to zero by repair, never by narrowing the model, and publish the count. Copy bare_truthiness_sites too and publish what it finds.
Publish your own blind spots. This primitive has them and they are in guardInventory.
thePrimitive.outOfScope: check-evidence-v10.py, check-retention-custody-v22.py and check-evaluation-proof-v11.py show indicative susceptibility on v5's own scan, and every checker in this corpus that parses JSON without an object_pairs_hook is susceptible to IR-C2V6-01. v7 does not repair them, does not grade them and does not touch them. RES-C2V7 carries no claim about those surfaces; the instrument to sweep them now exists and is reusable, which is the whole point of building it as a primitive. Adoption flows both ways: check-trusted-request-context-v3.py already had the duplicate-key defence v6 lacked, and this lane took it from there.
thePrimitive.theParseIsAGateToo: IR-C2V6-01. json.loads is not injective over bytes. jx_loads returns (value, problems): it repairs nothing and guesses nothing, it hands back the parse the host produced next to an explicit account of what the host threw away, and a caller that discards the account is visible in the caller's own source rather than invisible in the parser's. check-trusted-request-context-v3.py in this same directory already refuses duplicate keys by RAISING from an object_pairs_hook and retains a scored selftest row for it; v7 reports instead of raising, so the refusal is a NAMED FINDING AT THE POSITION and not an exit code, because a non-zero exit is not evidence a guard fired.
thePrimitive.orderingAndEqualityAgree: v6's jx_order reported EQUAL for 0.0 against -0.0 and for NaN against every float, both of which jx_equal calls distinct, and v6 disclosed only the equality half of that divergence. v7 does not disclose the ordering half; it removes it. jx_order decides the equal case by the same canonical string comparison jx_equal uses, before any < runs, and returns None - not comparable - for two distinct values of the same JSON type that do not order, which after this change is NaN and only NaN. The agreement is measured over the whole corpus cross-product on every run and published as primitiveOrderEqualityDivergences.
thePrimitive.howToStateTheNumericPropertyCorrectly: STATED ACCURATELY BECAUSE BOTH v6 DOCUMENTS STATED IT WRONGLY. v6 claimed 'no numeric operator is ever executed on a wire operand'. That is false as worded: jx_order runs `a < b` and jx_int_in_range runs `low <= value <= high`. The property that is true, and that is the one doing the work, is that NO COMPARISON BETWEEN OPERANDS OF DIFFERENT JSON TYPE IS EVER EXECUTED. Both of those functions gate every operand to the same JSON type FIRST, so no coercion path is reachable; `<` between two values already proved to be JSON integers cannot coerce anything. Equality never runs a numeric operator at all - it is string equality over canonical tokens.
thePrimitive.whatTheAdoptionStepsUsedToSayAndWhyThatM: v6's step 3 told an adopter to call jx_min and jx_max, NEITHER OF WHICH EXISTED anywhere in check-c2-v6.py, so following the normative instructions verbatim produced a NameError; and both v6 documents attributed to jx_sorted a refusal of heterogeneous JSON type sets that it does not perform - it orders them, and jx_sorted_homogeneous is the function that refuses. Adoption is one of this artifact's two declared deliverables, so a wrong adoption step is a live defect and not a typo. Both are fixed by construction here: jx_min and jx_max now exist and are real replacements for min and max rather than aliases for jx_sorted, the refusal is attributed to the functions that perform it, and check-c2-v7.py reads every jx_ name out of its own docstring AND out of this document on every run and emits a named finding for any that it does not define.

guardInventory.principle: Every guard has a blind spot. An inventory claiming total coverage is refused by check-c2-v6.py, which requires a non-empty blindSpots list on every declared layer.

layers.name: effective-contract integer type lock

layers.name: candidate-document total binding
layers.what: every integer leaf AND every JSON number leaf of THIS document bound to a value the run measured or to a byte of a hash-verified pinned input, with no unbound bucket, then probed with hostile spellings and arbitrary value drift; the float half is additionally probed live by inserting a JSON number at a key nobody binds, at the root and at depth.
blindSpots: it binds NUMBERS -- integers and floats. A closed STRING scalar of this document is bound only where the checker gates it explicitly (RES-C2V7-07). v6's version of this entry named strings as the neighbouring gap and did not mention numbers at all, while the entire artifact exists because of int/float equivalence, and the reviewer measured that a new leaf spelled 17 was refused and the same leaf spelled 17.0 reached a full green run. The gap is closed rather than reworded, and the wording is corrected too.
the binding table may be widened freely and narrowing it fails closed, but a binding pointed at the WRONG live key would be a wrong expectation consistently applied, and no layer catches that

layers.name: register totality
layers.what: the compared position set is derived from the live measurement and must equal the declared register in both directions; the inherited half must equal the predecessor's executed DECLARED_INTEGER_CONSTANT_IDS.
blindSpots: a counter that is published but NEITHER measured nor registered is invisible to L3; L2c is what closes that direction for this document
it registers positions, not semantics: a position registered under a misleading name is still registered

layers.name: inverted wire-comparison scan
layers.what: the whole function universe including lambdas and nested defs, a fixpoint taint model that propagates through comprehension, generator and container-constructor RESULTS, and the full operator space: equality, ordering, membership, key lookup, set algebra, dedup, aggregation and operator.* calls.
blindSpots: STILL SYNTACTIC. Its excusal test is textual and is not a dominance proof (RES-C2V6-01)

BARE TRUTHINESS IS NOT MODELLED AS A COMPARISON SITE. `if x:` on a wire number has exactly the int/float/bool equivalence semantics of `==`, and _hazard_pairs does not treat ast.If, ast.While, ast.IfExp, ast.BoolOp, ast.Assert, unary not or comprehension-ifs as sites. v7 adds the operator-space rows and MEASURES the sites over real source instead, publishing and binding the count; it is deliberately not a finding, because every site this run inspected is a container or a syntax-tree object where truthiness is emptiness. layers.name: behavioural type-fault injection and proof-honesty probes

blindSpots: exhaustive over REGISTERED positions only; it inherits L3's coverage exactly

blindSpots: only proves the repair differs from the predecessor where the predecessor is known-defective

layers.what: a float at EVERY integer leaf of the pinned predecessor document in turn, each mutant driven through a COMPLETE run of the pinned predecessor, recomputed on every invocation and bound. Not sampled.
blindSpots: it is evidence about the PREDECESSOR, not a property of this repair; L2b and L2c are the successor side

layers.name: successor differential against the REJECTED v5

layers.name: self-mutation
layers.what: breaks every declared type gate and every layer in copies of this file's own syntax tree, requires each break to be detected BY ITS NAMED FINDING at the POSITION UNDER TEST, re-runs each break against a candidate whose every bound counter has been republished from the mutant's own measurements, and additionally edits the candidate's OWN BYTES for the byte-level rows and executes the pinned REJECTED check-c2-v6.py over the eighteen-byte duplicate-key edit it was rejected for.
blindSpots: TERMINAL. A mutation battery cannot falsify itself; nothing stands behind it but independent review
the mutation set is finite and authored by the same lane that authored the repair, which is the structural reason an independent verdict is REQUIRED and is not replaced by a green run

layers.name: parse integrity
layers.what: the boundary between the BYTES and the parsed object, made a gate. Every JSON input this checker loads is parsed by jx_loads, which reports every duplicated key at its path, every non-RFC constant and every number token whose spelling is not the canonical spelling of its value; a structural scan requires every json.load and json.loads in this file to pass an object_pairs_hook, with two named and counted exemptions that reproduce the predecessor's parse as evidence; a behavioural probe drives fifteen hostile texts including three controls through the live parse and the live finding function on every run; and a differential re-executes, every run, the unhooked host parse that check-c2-v6.py performs, against three pinned documents, and requires it to be unable to distinguish the edited bytes from the unedited ones while this checker names the position.
blindSpots: STRING ESCAPE SPELLING IS NOT COVERED. `"a"` and `"\u0061"` parse identically and this layer does not object, because legitimate documents escape strings and a canonical-escaping rule would refuse them (RES-C2V7-08).

it does not reach the parses performed INSIDE the pinned check-c2-v4.py, check-c2-v5.py and check-c2-v6.py when they are executed as oracles; those are their own reviewed bytes and their blindness is what the differential MEASURES rather than a gap this layer closes

the full execution of the pinned check-c2-v6.py over the eighteen-byte edit is a --selftest row and is NOT recomputed by an ordinary invocation; an ordinary invocation recomputes the mechanism (RES-C2V7-11)

the candidate's digest is computed from the bytes this run read; it is not a defence against the file changing between runs, and this layer says nothing about any input the checker does not itself parse

layers.name: declared strings
layers.what: every finding id and every subject substring the retained assertion tables name is required to exist, in this file's string constants outside those tables or in the candidate document, and every jx_ name the module docstring or this document names is required to be defined. Both run on every invocation and not only under --selftest, because the two v6 defects of this shape - an assertion row asserting on text its guard does not emit, and an adoption step naming two functions that did not exist - were detectable only by running the whole matrix or by trying the instructions.
blindSpots: IT CLOSES 'NAMES A STRING THAT EXISTS NOWHERE'. It does NOT close 'names a string that exists SOMEWHERE OTHER than the guard it asserts on', which is the exact shape of the v6 row that asserted 'outside the census block' while its guard emitted 'OUTSIDE the census block', because the lower-case spelling genuinely occurs in a banner template. The emit-site figure is published so the size of that gap is visible rather than described (RES-C2V7-10).

the emit-site corpus is per-FUNCTION and a finding whose text is assembled across functions - anything routed through an escapes list - cannot be proved at its emit site at all, so a large part of the table falls back to the weaker module-wide corpus by construction
it checks that a named string exists; it cannot check that the string means what the row intends

guardInventory.whatStandsBehindTheBackstop: The adjudication's structural point was that in v4 the census layer WAS the behavioural backstop and nothing stood behind it. In v7 the comparison primitive has six independent things behind it with six different failure modes. L5 is behavioural and reads no source, so a source-level evasion of L4 does not reach it. L6 is anchored to EXTERNAL PINNED BYTES known to fail. L6b re-executes the predecessor over its whole document every run, so a claim about the width of the class degrades to a finding rather than to silence. L6c is anchored to the REJECTED v5, which still admits its own blocking vectors to a fully green run and cannot change because it is pinned. L7 breaks every gate and every layer and requires each break to survive republication of every counter. No single evasion satisfies all of them. The sixth is L8, which is anchored to the PINNED BYTES of the REJECTED v6 and to the host parser's own behaviour, and which no strengthening of the comparison primitive could have produced, because IR-C2V6-01 lives entirely below the comparison.
guardInventory.terminalLayerAndWhatStandsBehindIt: L7 is terminal and NOTHING stands behind it except independent review. That is stated plainly because the predecessor's terminal layer had nothing behind it either and did not say so, and the omission is what the adjudication graded BLOCKING. Every row is printed on every --selftest run precisely so that a human reviewer can be the thing behind it.

v7MeasuredCountersRule: Every integer leaf AND every JSON number leaf of THIS document -- not only this block -- is bound to a value this run measured or to a byte of a hash-verified pinned input. There is no unbound bucket: a leaf no layer binds is itself a named finding, so narrowing the binding table fails closed instead of silently exempting a counter. That is the repair for IR-C2V5-03, where thirteen of the v5 document's own integer leaves admitted a float to a full green run, and for OBS-C2V6-01, where v6's own totality enumerated integer leaves only and a NEW leaf spelled 17.0 reached a full green run while the same leaf spelled 17 was refused. The totality is over the PARSED document; the totality over the BYTES is L8, and IR-C2V6-01 is what happens when only the first of those exists.

residualAccounting.why: v6 was described to its coordinator as carrying ten retained residuals including the incomplete selftest. It carried seven, or eleven counting knownLimitations, and the incomplete selftest was never written into the artifact. These three integers are BOUND by check-c2-v7.py to the lists they count, so this document's account of its own residuals cannot be overstated in prose to anybody, including a coordinator.

residuals.title: L4's excusal test is textual, and the live hazard was never the excusal test
residuals.detail: A type gate excuses a comparison when a gate call with the same unparsed argument text appears earlier in the same statement, in an enclosing if/while test, or in an immediately preceding early-return guard. That is a textual proxy for dominance, not a dominance proof.
residuals.whyNotClosed: A sound dominance analysis over Python needs a control-flow graph and an alias model, which is a larger instrument than this checker and would itself need review. Carrying it unbuilt would be a paper seal, so it is retained open.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE v5's VERSION OF THIS RESIDUAL MISDIRECTED. The independent review measured that gate dominance excused exactly zero comparisons in check-c2-v5.py, so the '0 ungated' headline was produced entirely by the taint and non-numeric models and not by excusal at all. The number of sites this run excuses by textual dominance is published as scanSelfGateExcusedSites and is bound, so a reader can see the size of this residual rather than being told about it. The mechanism that actually hid IR-C2V5-01 was the taint model, which is repaired in L4 and probed by the SCAN_MUTATIONS row that injects the comprehension-result subset test verbatim.

residuals.title: L4's TYPE-ANNOTATION proof rests on an annotation the host does not enforce
residuals.detail: L4 excuses an operand when it is a parameter annotated str, bytes or ast.AST. Python does not enforce annotations, so a function whose annotation is wrong would have its operands excused.
residuals.whyNotClosed: Enforcing it would mean a run-time assertion at every annotated parameter of this file, which is a larger change than the proof is worth, and the alternative -- dropping the proof -- would flood the scan with sites that would then have to be excused by hand, which is how an excusal table rots.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: The sibling proofs are probed: every -> str function is CALLED over the JSON corpus by L5 and every result must be a str, and the AST-STR-FIELD proof is measured over this file's own tree. Only the parameter-annotation half is unprobed, it applies only to this file's internal helpers and never to a value that came off the wire, and L7 breaks the proof machinery.

residuals.title: v7 does not re-run the predecessor's contract-root execution matrix
residuals.detail: check-c2-v4.py --selftest drives check() over roughly twenty-four thousand mutated copies of the whole document and takes on the order of ten minutes. check-c2-v7.py measures the contract-root CENSUS but does not execute that matrix.
residuals.whyNotClosed: That matrix is the pinned predecessor's retained evidence at its own reviewed digest and re-running it here would duplicate rather than extend it, at a cost that would push this checker out of routine use. Naming it is not closing it.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: nothing in v7; this is a genuine coverage gap relative to the predecessor and is recorded as one. A reviewer who wants that evidence must run check-c2-v4.py --selftest, which is unchanged.

residuals.title: L2 trusts the predecessor's measurement functions
residuals.detail: v7 authors the COMPARISON and inherits the MEASUREMENT from check-c2-v4.py measure_surfaces, measure_contract_root and node_census. If those measured the wrong space consistently, L2 would bind a published number to a wrong number and agree with it. The primitive removes numeric coercion from the comparison; it cannot make a measurement correct.
residuals.whyNotClosed: An independent second measurement would be a second instrument needing its own review, and the adjudication explicitly confirms the leaf-inclusive measurement is sound and instructs that it be preserved, not rebuilt. The separation is deliberate but it is a trust relationship and is named as one.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: the predecessor's own independent review and the adjudication's execution-based confirmation of the measurement; not v7.

residuals.title: the type lock closes JSON type, not value, outside the bound registers
residuals.detail: L2c leaves NO integer leaf of THIS document unbound in value. The EFFECTIVE contract is different: L2 binds the counter register by value and L2b locks every other integer leaf by TYPE only, so a declared bound inside the inherited document could be changed from one JSON integer to another and no layer would object. The independent review of v5 measured exactly this at planIntent.wireTypes.stageBudgetV1.limit.maximum, where -1 and ten-to-the-sixtieth were both admitted.
residuals.whyNotClosed: Binding those by value would mean transcribing the predecessor's declared bounds into this document, which is the silent renumbering the brief forbids, or building a semantic model of what each bound ought to be, which is a second contract needing its own review.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: L2b for the type direction, L1 for anything the predecessor itself validates, and the derivation's from-clauses, which are bound to the verified predecessor byte for every path this document actually touches.

residuals.title: a checker cannot hash-pin itself
residuals.detail: check-c2-v7.py reads its own bytes once for the L4 self-scan and reports their sha256 in the banner. It cannot verify them against a digest it also carries.
residuals.whyNotClosed: Self-verification is circular. The digest is REPORTED so a reviewer can bind the verdict to bytes, which is what freeze section 7.2 actually requires.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: the reviewer, and the recording obligation.

residuals.title: law 18 names strings too, and the exhaustive document sweeps enumerate NUMBERS
residuals.detail: The primitive is type-exact for every JSON type and jx_bind_text applies it to closed string scalars, but the exhaustive document sweeps -- L2b, L2c and L6b -- enumerate NUMERIC leaves. L2c now covers both JSON integers and JSON numbers, which closes OBS-C2V6-01; L2b and L6b still enumerate integer leaves only. A closed STRING scalar spelled as a different JSON type is caught where the code gates it and is not swept.
residuals.whyNotClosed: The corpus's measured defect class is the numeric one: LB-C2-01, IR-C2V4-01 and IR-C2V5-01 are all int/float/bool equivalence. Widening the sweep to string leaves would multiply the run cost for a class with no measured instance, and claiming the wider property without sweeping it would be exactly the overstatement this artifact exists to close.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: the primitive itself, which is type-exact for all seven JSON types and is exercised over the full cross-product every run; and jx_bind_text, which every pinned-digest comparison already routes through.

residuals.title: the bytes-versus-parse class is wider than what L8 covers
residuals.detail: L8 covers duplicate object keys at any depth, the non-RFC constants NaN and Infinity, and number tokens whose spelling is not the canonical spelling of their value. It does NOT cover STRING ESCAPE SPELLING: `"a"` and `"\u0061"` parse to the same string and this checker does not object. It also does not reach the parses performed inside the pinned check-c2-v4.py, check-c2-v5.py and check-c2-v6.py when this checker executes them as oracles, nor anything in an input this checker does not itself parse.
residuals.whyNotClosed: A canonical-escaping rule would refuse legitimate documents - every JSON document in this corpus is free to escape a string and several do - and there is no measured instance of an escape-spelling divergence anywhere in the corpus, so the rule would cost real refusals to close a class with no observed member. Changing the pinned predecessors' own parses is forbidden: they are hash-pinned reviewed bytes and their blindness is the thing L8 MEASURES.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: for the escape half, nothing in v7; it is a genuine gap and is recorded as one. For the predecessor half, the differential, which recomputes the predecessors' blindness on every run rather than assuming it, and the recording obligation, which binds their digests.

residuals.title: bare truthiness is measured and published, not guarded
residuals.detail: bool(1), bool(1.0) and bool(True) are the same value, so `if x:` on a wire number carries exactly the int/float/bool equivalence semantics the operator space exists to enumerate. v6's 28-row table omitted it and L4's _hazard_pairs does not treat ast.If, ast.While, ast.IfExp, ast.BoolOp, ast.Assert, unary not or comprehension-ifs as comparison sites. v7 adds the operator-space rows and measures the sites over real source, publishing and BINDING the counts for this file and for the pinned check-c2-v6.py -- but it does not make them findings.
residuals.whyNotClosed: Every site the measurement reports in this file is a container or a syntax-tree object, where truthiness is emptiness and not numeric value, and this lane could not drive any of them to a false accept; the independent reviewer of v6 measured the same thing over the same model and reached the same conclusion. Making it a finding would mean either an excusal table with two dozen entries, which is how an excusal table rots, or rewriting every emptiness test in the file into a gate call, which would be a large change to closed code for a hazard with no measured instance. Carrying it as a bound measurement is the honest middle: the number cannot drift silently, and it is not dressed up as a guard.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: the operator-space rows, which execute the hazard and the primitive's answer on every run; the binding of both counts, so a change is a named finding; and the non-vacuity check, which requires the detector to report a positive over the pinned predecessor.

residuals.title: L9 closes 'names a string that exists nowhere', not 'names the wrong string'
residuals.detail: One v6 SOURCE_MUTATIONS row asserted the subject 'outside the census block' while the guard it asserts on emits 'OUTSIDE the census block', so it scored ESCAPE on the dispatched bytes. L9 would NOT have caught that, because the lower-case spelling genuinely occurs in a banner template elsewhere in the file. L9 catches the strictly weaker class: a declared string that occurs neither in this file outside the assertion tables nor anywhere in the candidate document.
residuals.whyNotClosed: Proving that a subject occurs specifically in the text the asserted finding id produces needs a data-flow analysis of finding STRINGS across functions, because a large share of this file's findings are assembled by prefixing an id onto escape strings built in other functions. That is a larger instrument than the property is worth and would itself need review. The emit-site figure is published instead, so a reader can see exactly how much of the table is proved at the guard it asserts on and how much only somewhere in the file.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: the full --selftest matrix, which is the only thing that detects this class completely, and which this lane ran to termination; and the published emit-site figure, which makes the size of the gap visible.

residuals.title: what an ordinary invocation does NOT recompute
residuals.detail: WRITTEN INTO THE ARTIFACT BECAUSE v6's EQUIVALENT WAS NOT. v6's residual list was described to its coordinator as 'ten retained residuals including the incomplete selftest'; it carried seven residuals, eleven counting knownLimitations, and the incomplete selftest was disclosed in prose to the coordinator and never written into the document at all. A residual disclosed conversationally is not retained. Accordingly: an ordinary invocation of check-c2-v7.py does NOT execute the pinned check-c2-v6.py. It recomputes the MECHANISM of IR-C2V6-01 - the unhooked host parse, against three pinned documents, plus the structural count of hooked parses in the pinned predecessor's own tree - and the FULL execution of check-c2-v6.py over the eighteen-byte edit, which must still be FULLY GREEN, is a retained --selftest row. An ordinary invocation also does not re-run check-c2-v4.py --selftest (RES-C2V7-03) and does not sweep string leaves (RES-C2V7-07).
residuals.whyNotClosed: Executing check-c2-v6.py costs about eighty seconds because it runs its own exhaustive 136-leaf predecessor sweep, and putting it on every invocation would roughly double the cost of a checker that is already about ninety seconds and would push it out of routine use. Putting it in the retained suite keeps it executed rather than asserted, at the cost of it not being executed by a plain run - which is stated here rather than left for a reviewer to discover.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: the per-run mechanism, which is anchored to the same pinned bytes; the retained --selftest row, which this lane ran to termination; and the residualAccounting block, whose counts are bound to the lists they count so that this document's own residual count can never again be overstated to anybody.

knownLimitations.thisIsNotAVerdict: A green run of check-c2-v6.py is authored by the same lane that authored the repair. It is checker-scope evidence. Independent re-review is REQUIRED.
knownLimitations.implementableIsNotDischarged: No property here is marked DISCHARGED or DEMONSTRATED on the strength of implementable: true.
knownLimitations.noStatusChanged: No seal, freeze, integration or product acceptance is declared. CD-RT-5 remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A.
knownLimitations.cost: The whole-document predecessor sweep is exhaustive on every run rather than sampled, which is the repair for a published figure the run did not recompute. The elapsed cost is published in the banner. The --selftest suite additionally executes the pinned check-c2-v6.py once, which costs about eighty seconds more, and the sweep-sensitive source rows clear the pinned cache and re-run the predecessor sweep, so the suite takes tens of minutes. It is not hung.
knownLimitations.residualsAreInTheArtifactAndNotInProse: Every residual of this candidate is in the residuals list above, counted by residualAccounting, and bound by the checker to what it counts. Nothing is disclosed to a coordinator or a reviewer conversationally instead of here. That rule exists because v6's incomplete selftest was disclosed exactly that way and never appeared in the artifact.
